title: Ali Fazal Plays a Cop Hunting a Child Killer in Raakh. It Drops on Prime Video June 12, Two Months Before He Returns as Guddu Pandit.
excerpt: Sonali Bendre makes her streaming debut in this investigative thriller. Director Prosit Roy calls it his most emotionally intense project yet.
body:
Ali Fazal is about to have the busiest summer of any actor in Indian cinema. On **June 12**, he arrives on **Prime Video** as a relentless investigating officer in **Raakh**, an investigative thriller about two missing teenagers. Three months later, on **September 4**, he'll be back on the big screen as Guddu Pandit in **Mirzapur: The Movie** — the first Indian streaming series to make the jump to theatrical release.

Two radically different roles. Two different platforms. One actor who has spent the last three years quietly becoming one of Hindi entertainment's most versatile performers.

## What Raakh Is About

The premise is deceptively simple and deliberately unsettling. **Two teenagers vanish without a trace.** A close-knit family is shattered. An entire city goes on edge. Ali Fazal's character — a methodical, obsessive investigating officer — launches a nationwide manhunt that pulls him deeper into a world of violence and human depravity.

Director **Prosit Roy**, who previously made the atmospheric horror film Pari and the critically acclaimed Paatal Lok, describes Raakh as something that "goes far beyond being a crime thriller." In a statement, he said: "What excited me most was the opportunity to merge the thrill of a gripping manhunt with an unflinching exploration of trauma and the darker impulses of human nature."

The show is co-created and written by **Anusha Nandakumar** and **Sandeep Saket**, with dialogues by Ayush Trivedi.

## Sonali Bendre's Streaming Debut

Perhaps the most intriguing casting choice is **Sonali Bendre**, who joins the series in a pivotal role alongside **Aamir Bashir**. For a generation of NRI families, Bendre was the face of '90s Bollywood grace — from Hum Saath Saath Hain to Sarfarosh to Kal Ho Naa Ho. Her return to the screen after battling and surviving cancer has been one of the more quietly celebrated comebacks in Indian entertainment.

Raakh marks her first major streaming role, and if Prosit Roy's track record is any indication, this won't be a soft landing. Paatal Lok was unflinching in its portrayal of caste violence and institutional rot. Raakh seems to promise a similar refusal to look away.

## Ali Fazal's Strategic Year

What makes Fazal's 2026 calendar particularly interesting is the contrast between his two major releases. In Raakh, he plays a law enforcement officer — measured, procedural, driven by a need for justice. In Mirzapur: The Movie, he's Guddu Pandit, arguably the most unhinged anti-hero in Indian streaming history.

The Mirzapur film, confirmed for a **September 4 worldwide theatrical release**, will bring back the original Season 1 cast including **Pankaj Tripathi** as Kaleen Bhaiya and **Divyenndu** as Munna Tripathi. Fazal has said the film is a standalone — designed to work for people who've never watched the series. "People who have not seen Mirzapur, it will work, and people who have seen it, the logic will fit," he told Bollywood Hungama.

## Why This Matters for Diaspora Audiences

Prime Video's global reach means Raakh will be available to NRI audiences simultaneously with its India premiere — no theatrical window delays, no regional licensing gaps. For the Indian diaspora, especially younger viewers who discovered Ali Fazal through Mirzapur and then watched him hold his own alongside Gal Gadot in Death on the Nile, this is appointment viewing.

The investigative thriller genre has been one of streaming's strongest performers in India. From Paatal Lok to Kohrra to Dahaad, the best entries in this space have combined procedural storytelling with searing social commentary. If Raakh follows that template — and Prosit Roy's involvement suggests it will — it could be one of Prime Video's strongest Indian originals of the year.

**Raakh premieres June 12 on Prime Video.** Mirzapur: The Movie hits theatres September 4.

*Sources: Bollywood Hungama, Filmfare, Sacnilk, Prime Video*
